name: Olivia Clark
occupation: Portland City Councilor, Council Vice President

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Clark was elected District 4 city councilor in November 2024 and began her term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 4 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

bio.statement: Clark's city candidate filing form lists past work as executive director of public affairs at TriMet.

source.publisher: City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections

bio.statement: Clark's filing form lists past work in legislative and intergovernmental affairs for Governor John Kitzhaber.
bio.excerpt: Legislative and Intergovernmental Affairs, Governor John Kitzhaber

source.publisher: City of Portland Auditor's Office, Elections

bio.statement: OPB reports Clark has been City Council vice president since January.
bio.excerpt: Clark has been council vice president since January, a position that gives her unique strategic oversight of the body.

positions.statement: OPB reports Clark's campaign priorities are improving police response and making the city more climate resilient.
positions.excerpt: Her campaign priorities are improving police response and making the city more climate resilient.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Clark was pivotal in passing the Transportation Utility Fee.
positions.excerpt: She was also pivotal in passing the Transportation Utility Fee

gaps: Voters' pamphlet statement not readable: the individual statement PDF in the county's Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide is a scan with no machine-readable text, and the full and large-print county pamphlet PDFs are cut off by the fetch tool (~105k characters) before the City of Portland section (pp. M-52 to M-66)
No policy positions stated on her portland.gov council page

verification_summary.balance_notes: D4: 6 items (3 T1, 3 T3) vs 8-12 for most rivals. Disparity is a confirmed source-access gap: her individual pamphlet statement PDF returns no machine-readable text, and the full county pamphlet text is cut off (~104k chars) before the City of Portland pages; her portland.gov page lists no policy priorities. Not unequal effort, but her campaign site oliviaforportland.com (confirmed on AUD-120) was not used as a T2 source and could fill the gap. Incumbent true confirmed (She/Her; Council Vice President).
